# Two lodash-es advisories ship inside the mermaid bundle, unreachable today by accident

## Context

Two open Dependabot alerts on `lodash-es`, both reaching us transitively:

| # | severity | range | patched | summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 97 | **high** | `>= 4.0.0, <= 4.17.23` | `4.18.0` | code injection via `_.template` imports key names |
| 98 | medium | `<= 4.17.23` | `4.18.0` | prototype pollution via array path bypass in `_.unset` and `_.omit` |

Nothing in `neomjs/neo` imports lodash. The path is entirely upstream:

```
mermaid@12.0.0 (devDependency)
├─┬ chevrotain@11.1.2
│ ├── lodash-es@4.17.23          ← vulnerable
│ ├─┬ @chevrotain/cst-dts-gen@11.1.2
│ │ └── lodash-es@4.17.23        ← vulnerable
│ └─┬ @chevrotain/gast@11.1.2
│   └── lodash-es@4.17.23        ← vulnerable
└─┬ dagre-d3-es@7.0.14
  └── lodash-es@4.18.1           ← already patched
```

Live latest-open sweep 2026-09-16T19:2xZ: no open ticket on either alert. A2A sweep of the latest 30 messages: no claim on dependency security.

## The Problem — "devDependency" understates it

`mermaid` is a devDependency, which normally ends the conversation. It does not here: **the bundle it produces is a published artifact.**

- `npm run bundle-mermaid` → `buildScripts/build/mermaid.mjs` → `dist/mermaid.mjs`
- `.npmignore:81` carries `!/dist/mermaid.mjs` — an explicit **negation**, so that file is published
- `src/component/wrapper/Mermaid.mjs` and `src/main/addon/Mermaid.mjs` load it at runtime

So the chevrotain code that imports `lodash-es` is compiled into an artifact every consumer of `neo.mjs` receives. The honest framing is not "we do not use lodash" but "we ship a bundle that contains lodash code".

## The Architectural Reality — and why this is not urgent

Measured rather than assumed, in both the tree and the shipped artifact:

**1. Chevrotain does not import either vulnerable function.** Its 27 `lodash-es` import sites pull 40 names:

> `assign clone compact defaults difference drop dropRight every filter find first flatMap flatten forEach groupBy has identity includes indexOf isArray isEmpty isFunction isObject isRegExp isString isUndefined keys last map noop pickBy reduce reject some uniq values` …

`template`, `unset` and `omit` are **absent**. It uses `pickBy`, not `omit`. The single `template` hit in chevrotain's source is the word inside a comment about template strings.

**2. The shipped bundle contains neither.** Against the built `dist/mermaid.mjs` (3.4 MB):

```
function template   0
function unset      0
function omit       0
baseUnset           0
```

esbuild tree-shakes what nothing imports, so the vulnerable sinks are not in the artifact at all.

**So neither advisory is exploitable through this path today** — not in `node_modules`, not in what consumers receive.

**That is a reason to patch calmly, not a reason to dismiss.** The tree-shake is an accident of chevrotain's current import list. A single patch-level chevrotain release that starts using `omit` would put a prototype-pollution sink into a published bundle, and by then the alert would already be closed as "not applicable" if we dismissed it.

**Upstream has moved, but we cannot follow.** `chevrotain@13.2.0` dropped `lodash-es` entirely — its dependency set is `@chevrotain/*` only. But `mermaid@latest` is still `12.0.0` and pins `chevrotain: ~11.1.2`, so the fix is unreachable by upgrading anything we declare.

## The Fix

An `overrides` entry, which is already this repository's idiom for exactly this shape:

```json
"overrides": {
  "gray-matter":    {"js-yaml":    "^3.15.2"},
  "monaco-editor":  {"dompurify":  "^3.4.13"}
}
```

Add `"lodash-es": "^4.18.0"` at top level rather than scoped under `chevrotain`. Scoped would need three entries — `chevrotain`, `@chevrotain/cst-dts-gen`, `@chevrotain/gast` — because a nested override only governs that package's own dependency. Top level covers all three and is a no-op for `dagre-d3-es`, which already resolves `4.18.1`.

4.17.23 → 4.18.x is same-major, and one consumer in this very tree already runs 4.18.1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `npm ls lodash-es --all` reports **no** version `<= 4.17.23`; the three chevrotain copies resolve `^4.18.0`.
- [ ] AC-2: both alerts close on the next Dependabot scan. Until then, the AC-1 output is the evidence.
- [ ] AC-3: `npm run bundle-mermaid` still produces a working `dist/mermaid.mjs`, verified by the specs that render it — `e2e/portal/LearnMermaidRender.spec.mjs` and `unit/component/MermaidTheme.spec.mjs`.
- [ ] AC-4: the `package-lock.json` diff touches **only** `lodash-es` resolutions. An override that quietly re-resolves unrelated packages is a different change.
- [ ] AC-5 — `revalidationTrigger`: the override is retired when `mermaid` moves to `chevrotain@13`, which needs no lodash at all. Recorded as a comment beside the entry, so removing it is a decision rather than an archaeology exercise.

## Out of Scope

- Upgrading `mermaid` — `12.0.0` is latest and pins the vulnerable range itself.
- Vendoring or patching chevrotain.
- The other `overrides` entries.
- Rebuilding and committing `dist/mermaid.mjs` — it is gitignored (`.gitignore:68`) and built at publish time.

## Avoided Traps

- ⛔ **Do not dismiss the alerts as "devDependency, not shipped".** `.npmignore:81` publishes the bundle; the code does reach consumers.
- ⛔ **Do not dismiss them as "not exploitable" either.** True today, and true only because chevrotain happens not to import those two functions. The measurement belongs in the PR body as the reason it is not urgent, never as the reason to close it unpatched.
- ⛔ **Do not scope the override under `chevrotain` alone.** Two of the three vulnerable copies sit under `@chevrotain/cst-dts-gen` and `@chevrotain/gast`, which a `chevrotain`-scoped entry does not reach.
- ⛔ **Do not let the lock diff sprawl.** `npm install` under a new override can re-resolve more than intended; AC-4 is the check, and a wide diff means stop and narrow rather than ship it.
